results.proposal_summary: Nature for Health (N4H) Phase II, funded by Germany (BMUV through IKI) with an initial contribution of €50 million, issued a call for Expressions of Interest targeting governments of ODA-eligible countries and regional intergovernmental entities to implement integrated, preventative One Health approaches addressing biodiversity loss, zoonotic spillover risk, and environmental determinants of health. Eligible applicants were national governments (including sub-national entities) and regional intergovernmental organisations on the OECD DAC list; non-governmental entities were explicitly excluded. Up to six proposals could receive seed funding of up to USD 2,250,000 each for 2–3-year implementation phases. The application window ran from 10 January 2025 to 7 April 2025, with selection anticipated in August 2025. Co-financing was not a general mandatory requirement but was needed when proposed activities extend to non-ODA-eligible countries. The call has since closed.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The call focuses on biodiversity conservation, One Health pandemic prevention, and environmental health — areas outside the ILO's core mandate of labour standards, decent work, employment, and social protection.

results.proposal_summary: The Malaysia-UN SDG Trust Fund CFP-2024/25, a partnership between the UN in Malaysia and Yayasan MySDG (supported by Malaysia's Ministry of Finance), issued a call for proposals in September–November 2024 to fund innovative, people-centric projects accelerating SDG achievement in Malaysia. The call targeted projects addressing marginalised groups across three pillars: People & Prosperity, Planet, and Peace & Partnership. Eligible applicants included Malaysia-registered CSOs, NGOs, academic institutions, and think-tanks (NUNOs) as well as UN agencies that are members of the Malaysia UN Country Team and have signed the Fund's MOU (PUNOs). Grants ranged from USD 100,000 to USD 500,000 per proposal, with project durations of 6 to 18 months. The submission deadline was 4 November 2024, and the call is now closed.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The call's priority areas include social protection for informal workers, decent jobs and skills training, and rights of marginalised groups — all core ILO mandate areas — though its broader scope also covers environment, biodiversity, and social cohesion beyond the ILO's core focus.

results.proposal_summary: The UK Home Office Modern Slavery Fund Albania Programme 2026–2029, administered by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office, invites proposals totalling approximately £3.24 million to reduce vulnerability to human trafficking among Albanian nationals and third-country nationals in Albania. The programme is structured across four lots: prevention, identification and reintegration, institutional development in Albania (Lots 1–3), and improving identification and referral of Albanian nationals in the UK (Lot 4). Eligible applicants are legally registered NGOs, civil society organisations, research institutions, UK-based non-profit organisations, educational institutions, and LMIC-based organisations; Lots 1–3 require a consortium of up to three organisations with a named lead partner. UN agencies and intergovernmental organisations are not among the eligible entity types. results.proposal_summary: The IKI Medium Grants 2021 was a competitive grant programme funded by the German Federal Ministry for the Environment (BMU) and administered by ZUG gGmbH under the International Climate Initiative (IKI). The call focused on two priorities: resilience of local populations in the context of COVID-19 and climate change adaptation, and development of participatory processes for ambitious climate action. Eligible applicants were German civil society organisations (NGOs, foundations, think tanks, universities, research institutes, non-profit enterprises) with at least one mandatory local implementing partner in an ODA-eligible country. Grants ranged from EUR 300,000 to EUR 800,000 per project for implementation periods of 24 to 36 months. The submission window ran from 25 February 2021 to 25 May 2021 and has closed; the selection process is complete with eleven projects under implementation. UN agencies and intergovernmental organisations were not eligible applicants.
results.ilo_match_evidence: While the call addresses climate resilience and livelihoods with some relevance to ILO's decent work mandate, it is exclusively targeted at German civil society organisations and focuses on climate adaptation and biodiversity rather than ILO's core labour, employment, or social protection themes.

results.proposal_summary: The IKI Small Grants 2020 was the 2nd call under Germany's International Climate Initiative (IKI), implemented by GIZ, aimed at funding small climate action projects. The application period ran from 8 December 2020 to 9 February 2021 and is now closed. The call focused on climate mitigation, adaptation, natural carbon sinks, and biodiversity conservation in developing and emerging countries. Grant size, eligible applicant types, and country eligibility are not specified in the available page content. This call is finished and no longer open for applications.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The call is focused entirely on climate change and biodiversity, with no connection to ILO's core mandate of labour standards, decent work, employment, or social protection.

results.exclusion_reason: The submission deadline (18 February 2025) has passed, and the call is no longer open — 375 outlines have already been received and are under review. Additionally, ILO eligibility is unclear as the call targets German and international grant recipients and implementing organisations of the German Federal Government, with no explicit mention of UN agencies or intergovernmental organisations as eligible applicants.
results.classification_summary: The IKI Thematic Call 2024 is ineligible because the mandatory project outline submission deadline of 18 February 2025 has passed, making this a closed call. The page explicitly states that 375 outlines were received and are now under review, confirming the call is no longer accepting applications. Furthermore, the eligible applicant categories (German and international grant recipients, implementing organisations of the German Federal Government) do not explicitly include UN agencies, intergovernmental organisations, or multilateral entities, so ILO eligibility cannot be established.

ILO Eligibility.evidence: The call is open to 'German and international grant recipients as well as to implementing organisations of the German Federal Government.' The eligible entity categories do not explicitly include UN agencies, intergovernmental organisations, or multilateral entities. The ILO is a UN specialized agency/IGO and does not fall within the named categories.

Funding instrument is grant.evidence: The funding announcement states 'projects implemented by organisations based in Germany and abroad receive funding through grants' — non-reimbursable grants confirmed.

Grant size above threshold.evidence: The funding volume per project ranges from 5 to 20 million EUR depending on the thematic priority, well above the USD 50,000 threshold.

Deadline is future.evidence: The deadline for submitting project outlines was 18 February 2025, 4 p.m. (CET), which is in the past relative to today's date of 2026-07-27. The page confirms 375 outlines were received and are under review.

Is open call with active application win.evidence: The call's submission deadline of 18 February 2025 has passed; the page confirms 375 outlines were received and are now being reviewed. The call is closed and no longer accepting applications.

Funding objective is ILO-implementable.evidence: Several thematic priorities explicitly focus on mobilisation of private capital, scaling innovative financing solutions, and business models — e.g., Priority 1 ('mobilisation of private capital'), Priority 2 ('business models for scaling energy efficiency'), Priority 4 ('innovative financing solutions for decarbonisation'). While some priorities (e.g., climate resilience, wetland conservation) could be programmatic, the call's central thrust includes private capital mobilisation as a key objective, which falls outside ILO's mandate as a technical assistance implementing partner.

Is procurement or tender.evidence: The call is structured as a grant-based ideas competition/project selection process, not a procurement or consultancy tender.

Requires cofinancing.evidence: Own funds/co-financing (criterion 8) are assessed positively but not stated as a mandatory exclusion criterion — it is listed as an assessment criterion, not a minimum requirement marked with '!'.

Requires specific accreditation.evidence: No specific pre-existing accreditation with another body (e.g., GEF, Green Climate Fund) is required. Eligibility requirements focus on legal form, turnover, experience, and consortium structure.

Has consortium leadership rules.evidence: The call requires application as a consortium (minimum two organisations). The lead organisation must meet specific requirements including turnover criterion, expenditure-based accounting (for German organisations), and 5 years of experience in ODA countries. No explicit rule stating the lead must be a non-UN entity, but the consortium structure requirements are detailed.

Applicant origin is restricted.evidence: The call is open to both German and international grant recipients, so applicant origin is not restricted to Germany only.

results.proposal_summary: The IKI Thematic Call 2024 is a grant competition run by Germany's International Climate Initiative (funded by the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action, the Federal Ministry for the Environment, and the Federal Foreign Office) to support large-scale climate and biodiversity projects in ODA-eligible developing and emerging countries. Nine thematic priorities were available covering energy efficiency, climate-friendly transport, industrial decarbonisation finance, forest and wetland conservation, coastal marine ecosystems, watershed resilience, and climate-security nexus. Grants range from EUR 5 to 20 million per project for up to 8 years. Eligible applicants are German and international grant recipients as well as implementing organisations of the German Federal Government, applying as consortia of at least two organisations. The submission deadline for project outlines was 18 February 2025 and has passed; 375 outlines were received and are under review.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The call focuses primarily on climate action, biodiversity, and environmental transitions with several priorities centered on private capital mobilisation and innovative financing — areas outside ILO's core mandate of labour standards, decent work, and social protection — though the climate resilience and just transition themes have peripheral relevance to ILO's just transitions work.

results.proposal_summary: Expertise France, under the WATANI programme, has launched a rolling grant window (NUMÜ) to fund organisations providing acceleration and business support services to existing Tunisian enterprises (startups, SMEs, and other businesses with at least 1 year of operation). The call is open from 14 April 2026 through 30 September 2028 on a rolling basis, targeting activities implemented in Tunisia. Grants range from €50,000 to €200,000 per project, with a maximum project duration of 24 months. Mandatory co-financing of 10–60% of total project costs is required, with sources excluding AFD, EU, and Expertise France budgets. Lead applicants must be legal entities established in Tunisia for at least 3 years with entrepreneurial support experience; foreign organisations may only participate as co-applicants. The ILO is not an eligible applicant type. Ineligible costs include loans, guarantees, VAT, land purchases, and direct financial transfers to enterprises.
results.ilo_match_evidence: While the call tracks job creation indicators in supported enterprises, its primary purpose is private-sector SME acceleration and enterprise support services in Tunisia, which falls outside the ILO's core mandate of labour standards, social protection, and decent work policy.
